tagline: Creek beds and salt licks give Dickenson County places their names.
intro: Skeetrock lies in Appalachian mountain terrain near the Kentucky border, in Virginia’s Dickenson County. Virginia’s byway program designates scenic roads that introduce travelers to alternative destinations.
Clintwood began in 1829 and was originally called Holly Creek, for the stream through town. Isom takes its name from Isom Mullins.
Clintwood is the county seat. Skeetrock’s name recalls skating on a creek bed; Bartlick’s combines a resident’s name with local salt licks.

moments.title: Clintwood
moments.text: Clintwood is Dickenson County’s seat, a town first known as Holly Creek after the stream running through it. In June 1948, Clintwood elected an all-female town council to serve until 1950. Nicknamed the “Petticoat Government,” the council tackled the practical business of town life: parking, garbage disposal and traffic hazards. It also organized a fire department and bought a fire truck. The work drew attention beyond Dickenson County. Lady Astor, the Virginia-born member of the British Parliament, expressed a wish to visit and see how the experiment was going; Voice of America featured the town in broadcasts.

moments.title: Skeetrock
moments.text: Skeetrock’s name came from a slippery creek bed where locals would skate, or “skeet.” This unincorporated Dickenson County community lies in Appalachian mountain terrain near the Kentucky border. Its post office opened in 1901 and remained in operation until 1958.

moments.title: Bartlick
moments.text: Bartlick folds two pieces of local history into one name: resident Bartley Belcher and the salt licks found in the area. It is an unincorporated community in Dickenson County, Virginia.
